questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Assesses practical policy design and enforcement in a real multi-tenant CNF gateway, focusing on OSS Gatekeeper usage, per-namespace configuration, and testability.

Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Rego policy referencing namespace ConfigMap values
- Per-tenant overrides via Namespace annotations/config
- Lightweight tests to verify enforcement
- Minimal YAML scaffolding for quick rollout checks

Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: defines RateLimitTemplate for K8sRateLimit
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sratelimittemplate
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRateLimit
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sratelimit
      # Pseudocode: reads per-namespace cnf.rate-limit and enforces a per-minute cap
      defaultRate := 100
      rateLimitPerMin := data.rateLimitPerMin
      # implementation would map namespace to rate and count requests
      # returns deny if burst exceeds rate
```

```yaml
# Constraint: per-tenant rate limit value
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sRateLimit
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rate-limit
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      kinds: ["Namespace"]
  parameters:
    rateLimitPerMin: 200
    targetPath: "/gateway"
```

```yaml
# Namespace manifest overriding default rate for tenant-a
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  annotations:
    cnf.rate-limit: "200"  # override default 100/min
```

```yaml
# Simple test pod to generate burst traffic for validation
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: rate-limit-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  containers:
  - name: curl
    image: curlimages/curl:7.85.0
    command: ["sh", "-c", "for i in {1..150}; do curl -s http://gateway-service/gateway || true; done"]
```

Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt this for token-bucket bursts and global vs tenant-specific ceilings?
- What are trade-offs of storing counters in-memory vs external stores for scale?

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests understanding of safe, per-tenant traffic experimentation without impacting production. It covers config-driven behavior, sidecar responsibilities, and end‑to‑end validation in a CNF gateway on Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts

- Traffic shadowing (mirroring) to a test shadow target
- Per-tenant configuration via Namespace ConfigMaps
- Fire-and-forget asynchronous forwards
- Deriving shadow path from tenant identity (X-TENANT-ID) and request path
- Observability: simple verification endpoint and metrics

## Code Example

```yaml
# Namespace ConfigMap (per-tenant) - cnf-shadow.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-shadow
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  cnf.shadow.enabled: "true"
  cnf.shadow.percent: "10"
  cnf.shadow.target: "shadow-svc.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local"
```

```yaml
# Minimal Deployment patch to mount config via envFrom (sidecar example)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: your/gateway:latest
      - name: sidecar-shadow
        image: your/cnf-shadow-sidecar:latest
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: cnf-shadow
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you ensure idempotent shadow requests if the shadow target replays on failure?
- What metrics would you collect to validate shadow traffic distribution and detect drift from intended percent?

```yaml
# Canary configuration ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: canary-config
  namespace: tenant-1
data:
  canary.json: |
    {"percent":20,"enabled":true}
---
# Sidecar deployment with ConfigMap mount
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: canary-sidecar
  namespace: tenant-1
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: canary-sidecar
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: canary-sidecar
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: sidecar
        image: canary-router:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: canary-config
          mountPath: /etc/cnf
      volumes:
      - name: canary-config
        configMap:
          name: canary-config
```

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simageprovenance
spec:

    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageProvenance
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8simageprovenance
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Deployment"
        some c in input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers

      }
```

```yaml
kind: Deployment
metadata:
```
